Not really feeling this one. The primary argument seems to be that member nations would have to hand over any information the WHA inspectors request of them, but given that requesting irrelevant information would be outside the mandates of the WHA, I don't see how this would be a problem. The other arguments are similar nothingburgers. 

On top of that, the repeal makes the confusing choice to both argue that members might not hand over any information except what is strictly required of them, *and* that the target is too intrusive in its demands, leaving me wondering whether the authors believe that nations should be required to hand over more or less information to the WA.

Isn’t Concerned a blatant veracity violation? The target allows the IAO to overrule a rejection under those conditions; it doesn’t grant the rejection itself under those conditions
What the repeal says doesn’t even make sense: why would you block release if there isn’t much harm in releasing?
That aside, astonishingly lazily written. 3 experienced authors and this is the result?
